agent.problem: Neither Gibeon nor Gezer has appeared in the earlier cards, and nothing in the setup lets the baker infer those place names. Both blanks therefore require luck rather than a reasoned understanding of the passage.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

human.problem: This two-blank card has no earlier context to reason from, so it can only be a discovery question. On top of that, even a baker who picks Gibeon and Gezer has no way to reason out which name goes in which blank, so the order comes down to luck. The docs allow 'a few discovery questions' but also say a blank tests 'meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.'
human.question: Can a two-blank fill in the blank be a discovery question when the order of the two right answers can't be reasoned out? Or should it become a one-blank card, or a multiple choice card with the pair as one answer?
